title: 第六章 看病的老郎中
content_zh:
那天的活，江砚干得格外艰难。

    肋骨的伤，让他每挑一担水都疼得冷汗直冒。劈柴时，斧头有两回差点脱手。王氏在一旁看着，非但没有半点心疼，反倒嫌他磨蹭，又骂了一通。

    捱到晌午，江砚实在撑不住，趁着没人，溜到村口一棵老槐树下歇脚。

    他靠着树根坐下，把怀里的秃笔摸出来，又摸回去。一上午，他脑子里翻来覆去都是那团发光的墨迹。可越想，越觉得没头绪——他连那东西是怎么触发的都摸不准，眼下更要紧的，还是没几日就要上门的那笔要命的债。

    正出着神，一个苍老的声音在头顶响起：

    “小子，脸色这么差，伤着了？”

    江砚抬头。

    树下不知何时停了一辆吱呀作响的独轮车，车上搭着个褪了色的布幡，上头写着个歪歪扭扭的“医”字。推车的，是个干瘦的老头，六十来岁，花白头发用根木簪胡乱挽着，一身洗得发白的旧棉袍，背有点驼，可那双眼睛，却亮得很，正落在江砚身上。

    这是个游方郎中。

    原主的记忆里，对这老头有点印象——姓秦，没人知道他大名，村里人都叫他秦伯。他不是本村人，每年入冬前后,会推着车在这一带的村镇间转悠，给人看看小病、卖点草药，换几个铜板或一口饭吃。秦伯医术不算顶好，可要价公道，遇上实在拿不出钱的，有时也就免了。在这缺医少药的边地，是个难得的好人。

    “没事。”江砚下意识地缩了缩，垂下眼，“摔了一跤。”

    秦伯却不走。他蹲下身，也不问江砚愿不愿意，伸出三根手指，搭上了少年的腕子。

    那三根手指又干又凉，搭上来的一瞬，江砚却莫名觉得，那触感里有种说不出的、令人安心的稳当。

    秦伯闭着眼，号了片刻脉，又翻看了江砚的眼睑，眉头慢慢皱了起来。

    “摔的？”他哼了一声，伸手在江砚后背几处伤上轻轻一按。

    江砚疼得倒抽一口冷气。

    “摔跤能摔出棍伤来？”秦伯收回手，浑浊的眼睛里透出几分了然，也透出几分这地方常见的、对苦难早已见惯的平淡，“肋上裂了一根，没断透，算你命大。再有这一身的旧伤……小子，你这日子，过得不轻松啊。”

    江砚没接话。

    秦伯也不再追问。他这一行走南闯北几十年，什么样的苦命人没见过。一个被打的乡下孤儿，背后是什么光景，他不用问也能猜个八九。
content_en:
Jiang Yan had an extremely difficult job that day.

    The injury to his ribs made him sweat in pain every time he carried a load of water. When chopping firewood, the ax almost fell off twice. Mrs. Wang watched from the sidelines, not only not feeling distressed at all, but she thought he was too lazy and scolded him again.

    When it was noon, Jiang Yan couldn't hold on anymore, so when no one was around, he sneaked to rest under an old locust tree at the entrance of the village.

    He sat down against a tree root, took out the bald pen from his arms, and then touched it back. All morning, the glowing ink stains were turning over and over in his mind. But the more he thought about it, the more clueless he felt - he couldn't even figure out how the thing was triggered. What was more important now was the fatal debt that was going to come to his door in a few days.

    While he was lost in thought, an old voice sounded above his head:

    "Boy, you look so bad, are you hurt?"

    Jiang Yan looked up.

    A creaking wheelbarrow parked under the tree at some point, with a faded cloth flag draped on it and a crooked word "medical" written on it. The person pushing the cart was a skinny old man, about sixty years old, with gray hair held up randomly by a wooden hairpin. He was wearing an old cotton robe that had turned white after washing. His back was a bit hunched, but his eyes were very bright, and they were falling on Jiang Yan.

    This is a wandering doctor.

    In the memory of the original owner, he had some impression of this old man - his surname was Qin, no one knew his name, and everyone in the village called him Uncle Qin. He is not from this village. Every year before and after winter, he would push his cart around the villages and towns in this area, treating people's illnesses and selling some herbs in exchange for a few copper coins or a mouthful of rice. Uncle Qin's medical skills are not very good, but he charges a fair price, and sometimes he doesn't pay for it if he really can't afford it. In this borderland where medical treatment is scarce, he is a rare good person.

    "It's okay." Jiang Yan shrank subconsciously and lowered his eyes, "I fell."

    Uncle Qin didn't leave. He knelt down and without asking Jiang Yan if he wanted to, he stretched out three fingers and put them on the young man's wrist.

    Those three fingers were dry and cold. The moment they touched them, Jiang Yan felt inexplicably that there was an indescribable and reassuring stability in the touch.

    Uncle Qin closed his eyes, took his pulse for a moment, then looked at Jiang Yan's eyelids, his brows slowly wrinkled.

    "Did you fall?" He snorted and reached out to gently press the wounds on Jiang Yan's back.

    Jiang Yan gasped in pain.

    "Can you get a stick injury from wrestling?" Uncle Qin took back his hand, his cloudy eyes showed a bit of understanding, and also revealed a bit of the commonplace in this place, which is already accustomed to suffering. "There is a crack in the rib, but it is not broken. You are lucky. And with this old injury... Boy, your life is not going to be easy."

    Jiang Yan didn't answer.

    Uncle Qin didn't ask any more questions. He has been traveling all over the country for decades, and he has never seen any kind of miserable people. He could guess what was going on behind a beaten country orphan without even asking.
title_en: Chapter 6 The old doctor who sees a doctor
